claims.text: An anti-corruption layer is code at the edge of a downstream context that translates the upstream model into the downstream one, so the upstream model's terms do not spread into the downstream model.
claims.source_hint: Domain-Driven Design (Evans), Maintaining Model Integrity: Anticorruption Layer

claims.text: At stage-2 OrderOwnerHandler checks IsInRole("staff") (line 22), reads FindFirstValue("sub") (28), passes it to ICustomerRepository.FindByIdentitySubjectAsync (29), and succeeds only if caller is not null and caller.Id == order.CustomerId (30-33).

At stage-2 OrdersController (CurrentCustomerAsync, 120-124) and OrdersV2Controller (27-28) read sub and call FindByIdentitySubjectAsync, then pass customer.Id to OrderService.PlaceOrderAsync(int customerId, ...) (OrdersController:41, V2:35; DonHang.Domain/OrderService.cs:15).

At stage-2 ICustomerRepository (DonHang.Domain) declares Task<Customer?> FindByIdentitySubjectAsync(string identitySubject); EfCustomerRepository finds the customer whose IdentitySubject (column identity_subject) equals it. Customer.IdentitySubject holds the sub of the customer's tokens.

At stage-2 a signed-in caller with no customer row (OrdersController comment: such as a staff member) gets 403 from POST /api/v1/orders (Forbid, line 35); in OrderOwnerHandler a caller without the staff role and no customer row is null, so Succeed is not called.
In ASP.NET Core authorization, a handler that does not call context.Succeed(requirement) leaves the requirement unmet, so the policy fails unless another handler meets it.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs: Policy-based authorization in ASP.NET Core, 'Why would I want multiple handlers for a requirement?' / What should a handler return?

claims.text: The Adapter pattern is one tool for building an anti-corruption layer; the layer's job is wider (words, values, rules) and it may hold several Adapter-pattern classes, or none: toward Keycloak the translation is one lookup inside the controllers and the handler, with no class that wraps Keycloak.
claims.source_hint: design judgement; outline item 4; Evans DDD, Anticorruption Layer (Facades, Adapters, translators)

claims.text: A translation layer must keep up with the upstream model; it pays off when that model differs from yours or changes outside your control, and conforming is cheaper otherwise. Here: a Keycloak user is not a customer (translate), role staff means Đơn Hàng's staff (conform).
Whether the layer runs as a separate service is a decision apart from the translation itself; in-process code is enough when the translation is small, as at stage-2.
Copying an upstream system's status text straight into your own data lets unknown values reach code that does not handle them; translating at one edge keeps them out.
